title: Silver Lane - retail prospect rapid notebook
content:
Quick scratch notes for Silver Lane (mid-market retail platform) outreach — raw, unpolished.

Context / why Silver Lane?
- Tech-first retail SaaS that recently raised Series B (press in Sept).
- They publicly talk about personalization and real-time product recommendations on their blog.
- Likely pain: cost of real-time inference at scale, latency spikes during peak traffic (holiday/weekend), and a desire to avoid vendor lock-in while experimenting with new LLM features.

Hypothesis / value props to surface:
- Redwood = predictable latency + cost controls for inference (talk about Dedicated & host fallback). Quick pitch: "keep personalization latency <50ms at peak without doubling infra".
- Private deployment angle for PII-sensitive customer signals (they likely ingest customer behavior). Emphasize VPC/on-prem options + KMS.
- Optimize for unit economics: batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions -> show example cost delta (rough ask).

Key people to reach (quick pass):
- CTO / Head of Engineering: likely decision maker for infra pilots. LinkedIn signals: "CTO: Arjun Mehra" (ex-ecom infra background).
- Head of Data/ML: productization lead for personalization. Search for "Head of Data: Priya Rao".
- Head of Platform/DevOps: ops champion for Dedicated/private.

Questions to validate on intro call (order of priority):
1) Current LLM/embedding use? (embedding provider, models, onboarded pipelines)
2) Peak qps for personalization generation + acceptable p50/p95 latency targets
3) Token volumes (per-day tokens / per-request average) — want to estimate cost impact
4) Data residency/PII concerns — need for VPC/HSM/KMS?
5) Existing infra: k8s + EKS? GCP? On-prem?
6) Pilot constraints: timeline, success metrics, stakeholders, legal/security reviews

Outbound subject lines to test (A/B):
- "Quick question on Silver Lane's personalization latency"
- "How are you handling inference cost in personalization?"
- "Pilot idea: 90% latency reduction at peak for personalization"

Initial cold email draft (short):
Hi Arjun —
I saw Silver Lane's blog on real-time recommendations and wondered how you handle latency/cost during peak traffic. At Redwood we help teams keep personalization latency predictable at scale while cutting per-token infra spend via batching, caching and Dedicated routing.
If you have 10–15 minutes next week I can share a 3-step pilot plan and a quick cost/latency sketch tailored to Silver Lane.
— Maya

Longer version (for follow-up / sequence 2):
Hi Arjun — following up. Two quick notes: (1) we ran a pilot for a retailer similar to Silver Lane and reduced tail latency by ~40% during promos using prefix caching + dedicated GPU pools; (2) we estimated 30% lower per-inference cost after simple quantization + smarter batching. No infra changes for the app layer — we provided an adapter that matched their existing API calls.
Would you be open to a short intro call + a cost sketch based on one week of logs?

Sequence plan (3–4 touches):
1) Cold email (above)
2) Short follow-up with 1-sentence case study + calendar link (3 days later)
3) LinkedIn connection + DM (1 week later) with a 1-slide image of latency/cost before/after
4) Final attempt with invitation to 20-minute "pilot brainstorm" (offer an NDA if needed)

Objection scripts (quick drafts):
- "We already use X provider and are committed." -> "Totally fair. We can run a non-disruptive pilot that sits behind your existing endpoints and compare tail latency/cost; many teams keep a fallback to their current provider during evaluation."
- "Security/legal will block third-party deployments." -> "We have a Private offering (VPC + on-prem packaged) and KMS/HSM integration; happy to sign an NDA and provide SOC2 report for initial review."
- "No budget right now." -> "Suggest a time-boxed pilot funded by Redwood or a revenue-share model for the first 6–8 weeks to prove value (we've done this with a few growth-stage customers)."
- "Not high on roadmap." -> "Propose a quick health-check call (15 min): we can audit logs and give a 1-page opportunity summary that their platform team can triage asynchronously."

Metrics to collect before pilot (ask for these in intro if possible):
- avg tokens / request, avg requests per minute (off-peak / peak), p50/p95/p99 latencies, % of requests that are cached or repeatable, cloud provider + instance types, monthly embedding volumes.

Pilot proposal skeleton (for a short deck):
- Goal: demonstrate reduced p95/p99 latency during peak + >=20% per-inference cost reduction without degrading relevance.
- Scope: 2-week technical eval, mirrored traffic to Redwood Dedicated, one critical endpoints (recommendation generation), engineer time: < 2 days integration + weekly syncs.
- Success criteria: p95 improved by X ms, per-inference cost reduced by Y%, no increase in error rate.
- Deliverables: test harness, latency/cost dashboard, integration guide, rollback plan.

Notes to self (to research before first call):
- Find Silver Lane recent infra hires on LinkedIn (platform leads) — prioritize people who mention "Kubernetes", "GCP" or "internal infra".
- Look for mentions of "personalization latency" or "real-time" in engineering blog posts.
- Prepare a quick cost model template (spreadsheet) where I can drop in tokens/day and get per-month cost delta between current provider and Redwood Dedicated + caching assumptions.

Open questions I want answered after first call:
- Are they running embeddings in-house or via third-party?
- Do they have hard latency SLOs for checkout / recommendations?
- How many environments (prod/staging) would need access for a pilot?

Next immediate actions:
- Pull Silver Lane press notes and Series B deck (if public) — Samir to help find investor slide with ARR and growth metrics.
- Prep 1-pager pilot template (Maya) + quick cost model (Ava) — due by next Wed 11/19.
- Send cold email to Arjun + connect on LinkedIn (target this Friday).

Random scratch items (brain dump):
- Offer: free 2-week smoke-test on Dedicated with limited token budget — see if legal will sign quick rpm.
- Potential champions: Head of Product for personalization (can push for pilot even if infra is slow).
- Keep outreach tone technical and concise. Avoid vague biz-speak.

End of notes.

(If this becomes active, move to shared_drives/go-to-market/ later — but keep this in users for now.)
